I am playing as p4 (grok-4.7) in this Monopoly turn.

I am evaluating my holdings and the opponent's position. I have just purchased NEW_YORK_AVENUE and hold an undeveloped yellow monopoly. I am checking whether p1 controls a full orange monopoly.

p1 holds St. James Place, Tennessee Avenue, and Kentucky Avenue. I now block their orange monopoly with New York Avenue.

p2 has two utilities, Pacific Avenue, and a GOOJF card. p3 has $691.

p3 holds a fully hotel'd light blue monopoly and owns Baltic Avenue. The green and red monopolies are split among the players. I control the dark blue pair with Park Place and Boardwalk.

I am deciding whether to build houses on my yellow monopoly. Mortgage Park Place for $175 would leave me with $726, which covers the $600 light-blue hotel. However, buying three yellow houses would cost $450 and leave only $101 cash. If I later need to sell those houses back, I would receive only half their purchase price.

Building any houses on the yellow monopoly would leave me short of cash. One house plus the mortgage yields $576, which is below the $600 needed for a light-blue hotel. I will not build and will consider trading instead.

I will not trade Park Place. p2 cannot afford the $1399 needed to buy three yellow houses and survive a light-blue hotel landing. Enabling p2's dark blue monopoly would be too dangerous.

I am weighing a trade for New York Avenue. p1 needs it to complete the orange monopoly and build houses quickly. I have no partial monopolies to offer in return, and p2 cannot provide anything useful either.

No trade can complete a monopoly for me. Unowned properties cannot be purchased during this post-turn phase. I will end my turn.

I mapped the board from New York Avenue. Rolling a 6 would land on B&O, an unowned property I could purchase for $200. Rolling a 9 would land on Water Works, giving p2 both utilities and a 10x dice rent multiplier. Light blue is behind me, so it is not an immediate threat.

Light blue is not an immediate threat this roll. I must complete a full circuit before landing there again. A Chance card could still send me to a property, but the probability window remains open.

I am checking whether any opponent can land on my yellow properties before I need the cash. p1 is at the electric company, p2 is at the reading railroad, and p3 is at a community chest. I am trying to determine p3's exact position after paying to leave jail.

p3 is on the Community Chest between St. James Place and Tennessee Avenue. They rolled a 7 from Jail to reach it.

p3 is two spaces before New York Avenue. From the Community Chest, p3 can reach Atlantic Avenue on a roll of 9, Ventnor Avenue on 10, or Marvin Gardens on 12. The combined probability of landing on any yellow property is roughly 22%. Undeveloped yellow rent is only about $5 in expected value, so building houses now would not be worthwhile.

Standard yellow rent values are now clear. Atlantic, Ventnor, and Marvin each cost $22 to $1200 depending on development level. With the monopoly active, undeveloped rent doubles to $44–$48 per property. One house yields $110–$120, two houses yield $330–$360, and three houses yield $800–$850.

p1 is at the Electric Company. Reaching any yellow property requires 14–17 spaces, so p1 cannot land there this turn.

p2 is also too far from the yellow properties to land there this turn. The only opponent who can reach them is p3, with roughly a 22% chance. Building one house on each property would cost $450 and yield only about $25 in expected rent from p3. Two houses on all three would require $900, which exceeds my available cash of $551. I am also checking whether I can build unevenly, since standard Monopoly rules allow a one-house difference between properties.

Even building rules likely apply, so a 1-0-0 house plan is probably invalid. One house on Marvin would yield only about three dollars in expected rent. I will keep my $551 cash buffer and skip building.
